record.title: Holomorphic structures in the low-discriminant non-algebraic case
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a non-algebraic complex surface and let $E$ be a differentiable rank-$r$ complex vector bundle on $X$ with $c_1(E)\in NS(X)$. Writing
\[
\Delta(E)=2r c_2(E)-(r-1)c_1(E)^2
\]
and
\[
m(r,c)=r\inf\left\{-\sum_{i=1}^r\left(\frac{c}{r}-\mu_i\right)^2\;\middle|\;\mu_i\in NS(X),\ \sum_{i=1}^r\mu_i=c\right\},
\]
determine whether bundles satisfying
\[
0\leq \Delta(E)<m(r,c_1(E))
\]
admit holomorphic structures. Any such holomorphic structure, if it exists, is necessarily non-filtrable.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/744), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Natural direct-limit C*-algebra for a general curved Hilbert manifold
record.statement:
For a general curved Hilbert manifold $M$ with Riemannian metric $g$, construct a natural direct-limit $C^*$-algebra
$$
\mathcal A(M)=\varinjlim_{M_a\subset M}\mathcal A(M_a),
\qquad
\mathcal A(M_a)=C_0(\mathbb R)\widehat\otimes\mathcal C(M_a)
\cong C_0(\mathbb R)\widehat\otimes C_0\!\left(M_a,\operatorname{Cliff}(TM_a)\right),
$$
where the direct limit is taken over finite-dimensional submanifolds $M_a\subset M$, by defining compatible connecting maps for smooth (isometric) inclusions $M_a\subset M_b\subset M$ so that the required diagrams commute.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/759), page 52. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Ground-state mass concentration for finite-time blowup of $L^2$-critical cubic NLS
record.statement: Determine whether every solution of the two-dimensional focusing cubic NLS equation (1) with initial data $u_0\in L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ and a finite maximal forward existence interval $[0,T^*)$, $T^*<\infty$, must concentrate at least the $L^2$-mass of the ground state, namely $\|Q\|_{L^2}$, as $t\uparrow T^*$. Here “concentrate” is used in the sense intended by the report’s preceding mass-concentration estimates, and $Q$ is the ground state defined by equation (5).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/764), page 30. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Eigenvalue sequences associated with finitely many nondegenerate curvature maxima
record.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth, bounded, simply connected domain, and let $H_h$ be the magnetic Neumann operator defined by
\[
H_h=( -ih\nabla-A(x))^2,
\qquad A(x)=\left(-\frac{x_2}{2},\frac{x_1}{2}\right),
\]
with magnetic Neumann boundary condition. If the uniqueness assumption on the maximum of the boundary curvature is replaced by the assumption that the curvature has finitely many maxima, each satisfying the stated nondegeneracy condition $\kappa''(s)\neq 0$, does there exist, for each maximum, a corresponding sequence of eigenvalues $z^{(n)}(h)$ as $h\downarrow0$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/767), page 31. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Homogenization of the stationary periodic Maxwell system
record.statement: For a lattice $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, let $\eta(x)$ and $\mu(x)$ be measurable, real, symmetric, $\Gamma$-periodic $3\times3$ matrix-valued functions satisfying $c_0 I\leq\eta(x),\mu(x)\leq c_1 I$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, where $0<c_0\leq c_1<\infty$. With $\eta_\varepsilon(x)=\eta(\varepsilon^{-1}x)$ and $\mu_\varepsilon(x)=\mu(\varepsilon^{-1}x)$, determine the behavior as $\varepsilon\to0$ of the resolvent $(M_\varepsilon-iI)^{-1}$ of the corresponding stationary Maxwell operator, including $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$-norm approximations for the electric and magnetic field intensities and inductions.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/767), page 47. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: The lattice covering problem in every dimension
record.statement:
For each integer $d\ge 1$, let $B_d$ be the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For a full-rank discrete subgroup (lattice) $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, define
\[
\mu(L)=\min\{\mu>0:\mathbb{R}^d=L+\mu B_d\},
\qquad
\Theta(L)=\frac{\mu(L)^d}{\det(L)}\,\operatorname{vol}(B_d),
\]
where $\det(L)$ is the absolute determinant of any basis matrix of $L$. Determine
\[
\Theta_d=\min_{L\subset\mathbb{R}^d}\Theta(L)
\]
and determine all lattices $L$ attaining this minimum.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/782), page 44. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: $L^1$-optimal Dirichlet boundary control of a string to rest in finite time
record.statement:
Given $T>0$, $L>0$, $c>0$, and initial data $y_0,y_1$, consider

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{u_1,u_2\in L^1(0,T)}\quad &\int_0^T \bigl(|u_1(t)|+|u_2(t)|\bigr)\,dt\\
\text{subject to}\quad &y_{tt}(x,t)=c^2y_{xx}(x,t), &&(x,t)\in(0,L)\times(0,T),\\
&y(0,t)=u_1(t),\quad y(L,t)=u_2(t), &&t\in(0,T),\\
&y(x,0)=y_0(x),\quad y_t(x,0)=y_1(x), &&x\in(0,L),\\
&y(x,T)=0,\quad y_t(x,T)=0, &&x\in(0,L).
\end{aligned}
$$

The report states that, under $T\ge t_0=L/c$, $y_0\in L^1(0,L)$, and $Y_1(x)=\int_0^x y_1(s)\,ds\in L^1(0,L)$, Theorem 1 explicitly describes all optimal controls, gives the minimum as $I(r)$ for a minimizing real number $r$, and states that the solution is unique if and only if this minimum is zero.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/02](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/783), page 25. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: The Big Z: optimal deterministic programming of POVMs
record.statement:
For a system of dimension $d$, a fixed ancilla Hilbert-space dimension, and a fixed number of outcomes $N=|Z|=|P|$, find the joint observables $Z$ that are most efficient for programming POVMs, namely those minimizing
\[
\varepsilon(Z)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_N}\min_{Q\in\mathcal M_{Z,A}}\delta(P,Q),
\]
where $\mathcal P_N$ is the convex set of $N$-outcome POVMs, $\mathcal M_{Z,A}=\{\operatorname{tr}_2[(I\otimes\sigma)Z]:\sigma\in A\}$ is the programmable set associated with $Z$ and ancilla state space $A$, and
\[
\delta(P,Q)=\max_{\rho}\sum_i\left|\operatorname{tr}\bigl[\rho(P_i-Q_i)\bigr]\right|.
\]
The report states that the solution is unknown even for $d=2$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/04](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/785), page 11. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Separability indicator criterion
record.statement:
For a Hermitian matrix $A$ admitting tensor-product decompositions $A=\sum_{i=1}^{r}B_i\otimes C_i$ into Hermitian matrices, let $m(X)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue of $X$, define
$$q_{B,C}=m\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{r}m(C_i)B_i\right)+m\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{r}m(B_i)C_i\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{r}m(B_i)m(C_i),$$
and define the separability indicator by $S(A)=\max q_{B,C}$ over all such decompositions. The report states that $A$ is separable if and only if $S(A)\ge 0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/04](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/785), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Unconditional instability of an explicit partitioned fluid–structure scheme
record.statement:
For the axisymmetric potential-flow/thin-elastic-tube model on $\Omega=\{(z,r)\in\mathbb{R}^2:0<z<L,\ 0<r<R\}$, with interface $\Sigma=\overline\Omega\cap\{r=R\}$, the explicit partitioned time-marching scheme obtained by discretizing the structure equation with leap-frog and the fluid equations with implicit Euler is unconditionally unstable whenever
\[
\frac{\rho_s h_s}{\rho_f\,\mu_{\max}}<1,
\]
where $\rho_f$ and $\rho_s$ are the fluid and structure densities, $h_s$ is the structure thickness, and $\mu_{\max}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the added-mass operator $M_A$. For the cylindrical geometry, $\mu_{\max}$ increases with the aspect ratio $L/R$ (asymptotically $\mu_{\max}\approx 2L^2/(\pi^2R)$ as $L/R\to\infty$).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/789), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Construction of functorial pull-backs in algebraic cobordism
record.statement: Construct functorial pull-back maps for algebraic cobordism for morphisms between smooth schemes, reducing to the construction for a strict normal-crossing divisor $D\hookrightarrow X$. For $D=(L,s)$ with support $|D|$, define the divisor pull-back on the modified cycle group by intersecting a cycle with $D$ when its image is not contained in $D$, and by factoring through $D$ when its image is contained in $D$. The report then states that the resulting triangle is well-defined and commutative, and that the canonical map from the modified cobordism group to the ordinary cobordism group is an isomorphism.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/821), page 30. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Unit-distance problem for translates of a convex body in the plane
record.statement: Let $t_2(n)$ be the maximum number of pairs among $n$ pairwise disjoint translates of one convex compact set in $\boldsymbol{R}^2$ that have mutual distance $1$. The Erdős–Pach conjecture stated in the report is that there exists $\\varepsilon>0$ such that $t_2(n)=\Omega(n^{1+\varepsilon})$. The same page states that the talk outlines a construction verifying this conjecture, and gives the stronger result $t_2(n)=\Theta(n^{4/3})$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/822), page 61. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Computing extension groups of rank-one MCM modules
record.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X=(x_{ij})$ be the generic $(n\times n)$-matrix over $S=k[x_{ij}]$, and set $R=S/(\det X)$, $L=\operatorname{coker}X$, and $L^{\vee}=\operatorname{coker}X^{T}$. Compute $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{R}(L,L)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{R}(L,L^{\vee})$, which arise from classifying extensions $0\to\operatorname{coker}Y\to Q\to L\to0$ with $\operatorname{coker}Y\cong L$ or $L^{\vee}$.

record.title: Percolating paths through random Poisson points
record.statement: Fix $d\ge 2$ and let $(\xi_i)$ be a rate-$1$ Poisson point process in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $s>0$, define $W_s$ as the minimum, over all $m\ge 0$ and all choices of $m$ distinct Poisson points $\{\xi_{j_1},\ldots,\xi_{j_m}\}\subset[0,s]^d$, of $m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}|\xi_{j_i}-\xi_{j_{i-1}}|$, where $\xi_{j_0}=(0,\ldots,0)$ and $\xi_{j_{m+1}}=(s,\ldots,s)$. The report’s Theorem 1(c) asserts that $W_s\to c(0+)$ in probability as $s\to\infty$, where $c(0+)$ is the common constant obtained from the equivalent formulations discussed in the report.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/23](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/828), page 10. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Concurrent Composition Using Super-Polynomial Simulation
record.statement: For any multi-party functionality, construct a secure protocol that remains secure when executed concurrently with multiple copies of itself and with other protocols, without assuming trusted parties, an honest majority, or network synchronicity. The construction uses a relaxed security definition in which the ideal adversary performs quasi-polynomial-time simulation, rather than polynomial-time simulation. Under the stated cryptographic assumptions— a hash-function collection collision-resistant against subexponential-size circuits and trapdoor permutations secure against quasi-polynomial-size circuits—the protocol has polynomial communication and computation and requires no setup conditions such as a common reference string or an honest majority.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/26](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/831), page 57. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: A Baum–Connes assembly map and reduced C*-algebra for loop groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a simply connected compact Lie group, and let $H=LG$ denote the loop group, with $LG$ understood in the report as the universal central extension of the group of pointed loops in $G$. Construct a natural $C^*$-algebra $C_r(H)$ encoding the positive-energy representations of $H$, together with an assembly-map isomorphism $\mu_H$ completing the displayed comparison diagram with the locally compact normalizer $N\subset H$ and making that diagram commute; in particular, the bottom-right term should be $K(C_r(H))$.

record.title: Density of embeddings of the maximal extension unramified outside \(p\) and \(\infty\)
record.statement: Let \(p\) be a prime, and let \(\mathbb Q_{\{1,p\}}\) denote a maximal algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) unramified outside \(p\) and \(\infty\). Determine whether the field embeddings \(\mathbb Q_{\{1,p\}}\hookrightarrow\mathbb Q_p\) have dense image. Equivalently, determine whether the associated conjugated homomorphisms \(\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}_p/\mathbb Q_p)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q_{\{1,p\}}/\mathbb Q)\) are injective.

record.title: Mixed boundary problem without the crease condition
record.statement: Determine whether the mixed boundary value problem for Laplace’s equation can be solved without Brown’s crease condition. In the report’s setting, \(\Omega=\{(x_1,x_2):x_2>\phi(x_1)\}\subset\mathbb R^2\) is a Lipschitz graph domain with \(\phi(0)=0\), \(D=\{(x_1,\phi(x_1)):x_1<0\}\), and \(N=\{(x_1,\phi(x_1)):x_1\ge 0\}\); the crease condition is the existence of \(\delta_D,\delta_N\ge0\) such that \(\delta_D+\delta_N>0\), \(\phi'\ge\delta_N\) almost everywhere on \(N\), and \(\phi'\le-\delta_D\) almost everywhere on \(D\).

record.title: Variable-coefficient oscillatory-integral estimates in the Bochner–Riesz range
record.statement: Let $T_\lambda f(z)=\int e^{i\lambda\phi(z,y)}a(z,y)f(y)\,dy$, where $(z,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\times\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 1$, $a\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^{2n+1})$, and $\phi$ is smooth on the support of $a$. Under the hypotheses that $\operatorname{rank}(\partial^2_{zy}\phi)=n$ and, for the unique $\theta\in S^n$ satisfying $\nabla_y\langle\partial_z\phi,\theta\rangle=0$, $\det\bigl(\partial_y^2\langle\partial_z\phi,\theta\rangle\bigr)\ne0$, determine whether the estimate $\|T_\lambda f\|_{L^q}\le C\lambda^{-(n+1)/q}\|f\|_{L^p}$ can hold for $q>(2n+2)/n$ and $(n+2)/q\le n(1-1/p)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/30](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1051), page 54. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Comparison of quotient norms for three analytic function algebras
record.statement:
For a function Banach algebra $A$ on $\[?]D$, define
$$
k_n(A)=\sup\left\{\frac{\|a\|_{A/m_\sigma A}}{\|a\|_{H^\infty/m_\sigma H^\infty}}:a\in A,\ a\ne0,\ \sigma\subset D,\ \operatorname{card}(\sigma)\le n\right\}.
$$
The comparison problem is to determine the growth of $k_n(A)$. The report considers $A=B^1_{1,1}$, $W$, and $B^0_{\infty,1}$, and states that in each case $k_n(A)$ is equivalent to $n$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1057), page 16. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Transcendence degree of the meromorphic function field of a Hermitian locally symmetric space
record.statement:
Let $X=G/K$ be a Hermitian symmetric space and let $\Gamma\subset G(\mathbb{Q})$ be an arithmetic subgroup, with $\Gamma\backslash X$ noncompact. Determine the transcendence degree of the field $M(\Gamma\backslash X)$ of meromorphic functions. The report explains that the Baily–Borel compactification $\Gamma\backslash X^{\mathrm{BB}}$ is a normal projective compactification whose boundary has codimension at least $2$; consequently, meromorphic functions extend to the compactification and
\[
\operatorname{trdeg} M(\Gamma\backslash X)=\dim(\Gamma\backslash X).
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/39](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1060), page 26. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Network design and facility location with service capacities
record.statement: Given a metric space $(V,c)$, a set $D\subseteq V$ of terminals/customers, demands $d:D\to\mathbb{R}_+$, a facility opening cost $f\in\mathbb{R}_+$, and a capacity $u\in\mathbb{R}_+$, find a partition $D=D_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}D_k$ and Steiner trees $T_i$ for $D_i$ $(i=1,\ldots,k)$ satisfying $c(E(T_i))+d(D_i)\le u$ for $i=1,\ldots,k$, such that $\sum_{i=1}^k c(E(T_i))+kf$ is minimum.

record.title: Switching/shunting problem
record.statement: Given a set of stacks of a given maximum depth (tracks); an ordered list of items (cars), one for each stack; a set of sets of items, with each set identified by its color (requests), where some items may remain uncolored (not requested); and one dedicated stack called the train, allowed moves are to move groups of items from the top of a stack to the top of the train, or from the top of the train to the top of a stack, preserving orderings. No stack may contain more items than allowed by the maximum depth. The problem is to finally have some stack that contains all colored items, consecutively, separated by color, and on the top of that stack, so that no uncolored items block access to the colored items. The objective is to minimize the number of moves.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1111), page 65. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Even/odd parity assignment equality problem
record.statement:
Given a matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, with the report’s convention $\mathbb R:=\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}$, let $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $P_n^+$ and $P_n^-$ denote the even and odd permutations of $N$, and define $w(A,\pi)=\sum_{i\in N}a_{i,\pi(i)}$. Determine whether
\[
\max_{\pi\in P_n^+} w(A,\pi)=\max_{\pi\in P_n^-} w(A,\pi).
\]
The report identifies this question with the even cycle problem.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1111), page 84. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Newton’s Proposition Six: velocity of the intersection of two moving curves
record.statement: Let two curves \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) move so that they continuously intersect at \(a\), and let \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) be representatives of the velocities of the two curves, represented in the figure by \(ab\) and \(ad\), respectively. In Newton’s construction, using lines parallel to the tangents of the two curves at \(a\) and the intersection point \(c\) specified in Figure 3, the segment \(ac\) is a representative of the velocity of the instantaneous intersection point \(a\). Equivalently, the problem is to determine the velocity of that instantaneous point of intersection from the two curve velocities and their tangent directions.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1117), page 12. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Quadratic-size Sidon-type construction for equivelar surfaces
record.statement: Given the cyclic construction on the vertex set $\mathbb Z_N$ with face vertices given by the cyclic translates of $0,A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_{2m}$ and successive differences $a_1,a_1,a_2,a_2,\ldots,a_m,a_m$, can the parameters be chosen so that $A_{2m}=\sum_{i=1}^m 2a_i=O(m^2)$ while the required intersection property holds? Equivalently, can one construct numbers $a_i$ (respectively $A_i$) such that all differences $A_i-A_j$ are distinct, except for $A_{2k-1}-A_{2k-2}=A_{2k}-A_{2k-1}=a_k$?

record.title: Existence classification for an unresolved Einstein–scalar-field Lichnerowicz class
record.statement:
For compact \a0$n$-dimensional manifolds, determine whether the Einstein–scalar-field Lichnerowicz equation

$$
\Delta_\gamma\phi-R_{\gamma,\psi}\phi+A_{\gamma,W,\pi}\phi^{-\frac{3n-2}{n-2}}-B_{\tau,\psi}\phi^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}}=0,
$$

has a positive solution for conformal data in the class
$$Y_\psi([\gamma])>0,\qquad A_{\gamma,W,\pi}\not\equiv 0,\qquad B_{\tau,\psi}\le 0,$$
where $W$ satisfies the associated momentum equation. The report’s Table 2 labels this class “NR” (no results indicating existence or non-existence).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/02](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1184), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Counting homomorphisms to a fixed directed acyclic graph
record.statement: For a fixed directed acyclic graph $H$, given an input directed graph $G$, determine the number of homomorphisms from $G$ to $H$, where a homomorphism is a function from $V(G)$ to $V(H)$ that maps every directed edge of $G$ to a directed edge of $H$. The report states that this problem has a dichotomy: for some digraphs $H$ it is in $\text{P}$, and for the remaining digraphs $H$ it is $\text{\23P}$-complete.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/07](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1189), page 68. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Optimal-control interpolation between falling-cat flip models
record.statement: Construct relatively simple falling-cat motions between the rigid Kane–Scher model and the alternative, more acrobatic flip model, using an optimal-control formulation with several contributing costs. The proposed costs are: elapsed time, weighted heavily; relative motion of the front and back halves, with severe spinal bending and twisting penalized while small-to-moderate relative motions are low-cost; changes in the shapes of the body components, represented by variations in their moments of inertia, with moderate changes relatively inexpensive and large changes expensive; and working blind, with inability to see the ground penalized while moderate deviation from the final head position has a low penalty.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/14](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1196), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Classification of simple modules for cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type $G(r,p,n)$
record.statement: For integers $r,p,n>2$ with $p\mid r$, let $d=r/p$, let $A=\mathbb{C}[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_d^{\pm1},q^{\pm1}]$, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and let $H(K)=H^{G(r,p,n)}_{\mathbf{x},q}(K)$ be the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,p,n)$. Given a specialization $\theta:A\to\mathbb{C}$ and the specialized algebra $H(\mathbb{C})=H^{G(r,p,n)}_{\theta(\mathbf{x}),\theta(q)}(\mathbb{C})$, determine a classification of the simple $H(\mathbb{C})$-modules.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/15](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1265), page 10. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: A complete renormalization-group trajectory between two fixed points
record.statement:
For the three-dimensional $\phi^4_{3,\varepsilon}$ Euclidean quantum field theory with sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, construct a double-sided sequence $s=(g_n,\mu_n,R_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ solving
\[
\begin{cases}
g_{n+1}=L^{\varepsilon}g_n-L^{2\varepsilon}a(L,\varepsilon)g_n^2+\xi_{g,n}(g_n,\mu_n,R_n),\\
\mu_{n+1}=L^{(3+\varepsilon)/2}\mu_n+\xi_{\mu,n}(g_n,\mu_n,R_n),\\
R_{n+1}=L_n(R_n)+\xi_{R,n}(g_n,\mu_n,R_n),
\end{cases}
\]
with
\[
\lim_{n\to-\infty}(g_n,\mu_n,R_n)=(0,0,0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\lim_{n\to+\infty}(g_n,\mu_n,R_n)=(g_*,\mu_*,R_*),
\]
where $(g_*,\mu_*,R_*)$ is the nontrivial infrared fixed point described in the report.

record.title: Determine the inner automorphism in the antipode formula for noetherian AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a noetherian AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebra of injective dimension $d$, with the notation of Corollary 9. If $\tau^\ell_\pi$ and $\tau^r_\pi$ are respectively the left and right winding automorphisms associated with the one-dimensional representation $\pi$ afforded by the right action on the left integral, then Corollary 9 gives an inner automorphism $\gamma$ of $A$ such that
\[
S^4=\gamma\circ\tau^r_\pi\circ(\tau^\ell_\pi)^{-1}.
\]
Determine $\gamma$.

record.title: Serre functor on the bounded derived category of equivariant perverse sheaves
record.statement: Determine the Serre functor of $D^b(\operatorname{Perv}_B(G/B))$, where $G=\operatorname{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$, $B$ is the Borel subalgebra of all upper-triangular matrices, and $\operatorname{Perv}_B(G/B)$ is the category of $B$-equivariant perverse sheaves on the flag variety $G/B$. record.title: Teichmüller ζ-functions
record.statement:
Let $d$ denote the Teichmüller distance and let $MC$ denote the mapping class group of some surface of finite type. Consider the ζ-type function
\[
\sum_{\gamma\in MC} e^{-s d(x,\gamma x)}.
\]
Find the critical exponent $s$, i.e. find the smallest $s$ for which this series converges. Does the series converge at the critical exponent? If the series does indeed converge, is the associated measure equivalent to Lebesgue measure? One might also reasonably ask these same questions for subgroups of $MC$.

record.title: Attainability of variational solutions for degenerate elliptic equations
record.statement: Let \(\rho\ge 0\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), with \(\rho,\rho^{-1}\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)\), and let \(A\) be a measurable symmetric matrix satisfying \(\lambda |\xi|^2\le A(x)\xi\cdot\xi\le \lambda^{-1}|\xi|^2\) for all \(\xi\in\mathbb R^d\), with \(\lambda>0\). For \(f\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\), consider \(-\operatorname{div}(\rho A\nabla u)+\rho u=f\). Define \(W=\{u\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d):\int_{\mathbb R^d}(u^2+|\nabla u|^2)\rho\,dx<\infty\}\), let \(H\) be the closure of \(C_0^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\) in \(W\), and let \(H\subseteq V\subseteq W\). A \(V\)-solution is a function \(u\in V\) satisfying the weak identity for every test function in \(V\). Is every variational solution attainable, namely obtainable as the weak limit of solutions corresponding to approximating weights \(\rho_h\) with \(\rho_h,\rho_h^{-1}\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)\), \(\rho_h\to\rho\) and \(\rho_h^{-1}\to\rho^{-1}\) in \(L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)\)?

record.title: Stable ROI reconstruction for internal components of region $A$
record.statement:
Under the report’s 2D ROI-tomography setup, with convex support $
$\Omega\subset\Omega_+$, measured-line set $M$, unavailable-line set $N$, region $A=\Omega_+\setminus B$, and $B=\{x\in\Omega_+:x\in L\text{ for some }L\in N\}$, determine a general stable-reconstruction result for internal connected components of $A$ (those not intersecting the frontier $\Omega_F=\Omega_+\setminus\Omega$). record.title: Convergence of a level-set evolution for simultaneous reservoir-shape and permeability reconstruction
record.statement:
Find forcing terms $f,h_i,h_e$ in the evolution laws
\[
\frac{d\psi}{d\tau}=f(x,\tau,\psi,\ldots),\qquad
\frac{dK_i}{d\tau}=h_i(x,\tau,\psi,\ldots),\qquad
\frac{dK_e}{d\tau}=h_e(x,\tau,\psi,\ldots),
\]
such that the evolution converges to the desired solution of the inverse problem: find a level-set function $\psi(x)$ and internal permeability profiles $K_i(x)$ and $K_e(x)$ for which the cost functional
\[
J(K_e,K_i,\psi)=\frac12\|R(K(K_e,K_i,\psi))\|_2^2,
\qquad R(K)=A(K)-g,
\]
is minimized, with
\[
K(x)=\begin{cases}K_i(x),&\psi(x)\le 0,\\ K_e(x),&\psi(x)>0.\end{cases}
\]

record.title: Higher-order Arf invariant for the Bing double of the Figure-eight knot
record.statement: Let $L=l_1\cup l_2\subset S^3$ be the Bing double of the Figure-eight knot. The link $L$ bounds in $B^4$ two embedded disks $D_i$ bounded by $l_i$, an immersed order-$1$ Whitney disk $W(1,2)$ pairing the intersections between $D_1$ and $D_2$, and a Whitney disk $W((1,2),(1,2))$ pairing the self-intersections of $W(1,2)$. This order-$3$ Whitney disk has a single interior intersection with $W(1,2)$. The problem is to determine whether this intersection represents a nontrivial concordance invariant of $L$ (as conjectured in the report).

record.title: Determining the critical inverse temperature for directed polymers
record.statement:
For the directed polymer model with simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and i.i.d., non-constant environment variables $\eta(n,x)$ having finite exponential moments, the free energy is
$$
p(\beta)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\ln\!\left(\frac{Z_n(\beta)}{Q[Z_n(\beta)]}\right),
$$
where $Z_n(\beta)=P[\exp(\beta H_n(\omega))]$ and $H_n(\omega)=\sum_{j=1}^n\eta(j,\omega_j)$. Given that there is a critical value $\beta_c\in[0,\infty]$ satisfying $p(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\in[0,\beta_c]$ and $p(\beta)<0$ for $\beta>\beta_c$, determine or characterize $\beta_c$.

record.title: Cohomology classes of singularity and multisingularity loci for families of maps of curves
record.statement:
Given a diagram of complex nonsingular varieties
$$
X \xrightarrow{f} Y,\qquad X\xrightarrow{p}B,\qquad Y\xrightarrow{q}B,
$$
with $\dim X=\dim Y=\dim B+1$, each fiber of $p$ a nodal complex curve, each fiber of $q$ smooth, $f$ proper, and $p$ restricted to the critical set of $f$ proper, assume that the family is generic: the restriction to each fiber has only isolated singularities and the deformations supplied by the family are versal. For the singularity loci $A_m(X)$, where locally the fiberwise map is $z\mapsto z^{m+1}$, and the multisingularity loci $A_{m_1,\ldots,m_r}(Y)$, defined by distinct preimages with singularity types $A_{m_1},\ldots,A_{m_r}$, determine their Poincaré-dual cohomology classes.

record.title: Relative-entropy regularization of Lévy-model calibration
record.statement:
Given market option prices $C^M(T_i,K_i)$ for $(T_i,K_i)_{i\in I}$, weights $w_i$, and a reference Lévy process $P(\sigma_P,\nu_P,\gamma_P)$, find a risk-neutral Lévy process $Q(\sigma,\nu)$ minimizing
$$J(Q)=E(Q)+\alpha I(Q\mid P),$$
where
$$E(Q)=\sum_{i\in I}w_i\bigl(C^Q(T_i,K_i)-C^M(T_i,K_i)\bigr)^2$$
and
$$I(Q\mid P)=E_P\!\left[\frac{dQ}{dP}\log\frac{dQ}{dP}\right].$$
The report states that the regularized problem always admits a solution, although the solution need not be unique; its solutions are continuous with respect to the input data and the prior Lévy measure, with further convergence to solutions of the initial calibration problem under specified conditions.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1389), page 26. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Isomorphism classification for the class $M_2$
record.statement: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for two algebras in $M_2$ to be isomorphic, where $M_2$ is the class of Lie algebras satisfying conditions (1)–(4) of Theorem 1: for an untwisted affine Lie algebra $g$ and a diagram automorphism $\tau$ of its centreless core $g_{cc}$, the algebras are of the form $L(g_{cc},\tau)$. The report answers this as follows: if $g_i$ are untwisted affine Lie algebras and $\tau_i$ are diagram automorphisms of $(g_i)_{cc}$, then $L((g_1)_{cc},\tau_1)\cong L((g_2)_{cc},\tau_2)$ implies $g_1\cong g_2$; for fixed $g$, $L(g_{cc},\tau_1)\cong L(g_{cc},\tau_2)$ if and only if $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ are conjugate in the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram of $g$.

record.title: Minimum degree of a nonzero difference of powers
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a ground field of characteristic zero, and let $P,Q$ be monic polynomials over $k$. When the top degrees cancel, so that $m\deg P=n\deg Q$, the report asks for an estimate of the minimum possible degree of the nonzero polynomial $P^m-Q^n$ in terms of the total number $r$ of distinct roots of $P$ and $Q$ in an algebraic closure of $k$. It states that the drop from the common top degree is at most $r-1$, equivalently
\[
\deg(P^m-Q^n)\ge m\deg P-r+1.
\]
It also states that this lower bound is optimal when $\deg P$ and $\deg Q$ are relatively prime.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1452), page 53. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Maximum number of $k$-edges in a planar point set
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of $n\ge 3$ points in the affine plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three collinear. For an integer parameter $k$, a $k$-edge of $S$ is a directed segment $pq$, spanned by two points of $S$, such that exactly $k$ points of $S$ lie to the right of the line through $pq$. Let $e_k(S)$ be the number of $k$-edges of $S$, and define
\[
e_k(n):=\max_{\lvert S\rvert=n} e_k(S).
\]
What is the maximum number $e_k(n)$ of $k$-edges that a set of $n$ points in the plane can have?

record.title: Optical tomography on simple Riemannian manifolds
record.statement:
Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded open domain with smooth boundary and let $g$ be a Riemannian metric on $M$. For particles of unit speed, let $f$ satisfy
\[
-Df(x,v)-\sigma_a(x,v)f(x,v)+\int_{\Omega_xM}k(x,v',v)f(x,v')\,dv'_x=0,
\]
where $\Omega_xM$ is the unit tangent sphere at $x$, $D$ is differentiation along the geodesic flow of $g$, $\sigma_a$ is the absorption coefficient, and $k$ is the scattering kernel. With incoming and outgoing bundles
\[
\Gamma_\pm=\{(x,v)\in\Omega M:x\in\partial M,\ \pm\langle v,\nu\rangle>0\},
\]
and albedo operator $A f_-=f|_{\Gamma_+}$ for the solution with $f|_{\Gamma_-}=f_-$, determine uniquely $\sigma_a$ and $k$ from knowledge of $A$.
